Chapter 7: Communicating Needs Clearly and Listening Deeply
Let’s take a closer look at something that truly shapes the heart of every strong relationship—communication.
Once you’ve started to get a handle on your emotional triggers, the next step is learning how to share what you need, and really hearing what your partner has to say in return.
Why does this matter so much? Because clear and honest communication helps you understand each other better, reduces those frustrating misunderstandings, and, ultimately, draws you closer together.
It all starts with self-awareness. You can’t share what you want unless you’re clear with yourself first. Take a moment to check in—what do you truly need right now?
Once you know, the next step is expressing it directly and kindly. Instead of hoping your partner will just “get it,” try something like, “I feel overwhelmed and could use some help.”
See how much clearer that is than dropping hints or expecting them to read your mind?
But here’s the other side of the coin—listening. And not just hearing the words, but actually tuning in with your whole self. That means putting away distractions, letting go of judgment, and focusing on understanding before you jump in with your own response.
Deep listening is about being present—physically and emotionally—and letting your partner know that what they feel matters, even if you don’t always agree.
So, how can you put this into practice?
Here’s a simple framework you can try:
First, use “I” statements. Say things like, “I feel… when…” to express your feelings and needs, instead of blaming or accusing.
Next, ask open-ended questions. For example, “How do you feel about…?” This invites real conversation, not just yes or no answers.
And finally, reflect back what you’ve heard. Something like, “What I’m hearing is that you’d like more time together—did I get that right?” This makes sure you’re both on the same page.
Imagine you’re feeling disconnected because you haven’t spent much time with your partner lately. Instead of letting resentment build, you might say, “I feel disconnected when we don’t have time for each other. Can we find a way to prioritize this?”
This simple shift opens the door for teamwork, instead of turning the issue into a battleground.
Deep listening also means being open to hearing things that might be tough—and responding with empathy, not defensiveness.
When both partners feel truly heard and understood, trust grows, and your relationship becomes a safe place for honesty and vulnerability.
So, what are the guiding principles to keep in mind?
Be clear and honest—this keeps resentment and confusion at bay.
Remember, deep listening is just as important as sharing your truth.
And above all, empathy is what bridges your differences and brings you closer together.
By mastering these skills—clear communication and deep listening—you’ll build a relationship where both you and your partner feel truly valued and understood.
